input:
You write the way in: what is said while a frozen video turns into an ad. It must make people stay for the ad.
Frozen moment at 4.7s: Kitten is sharp and looking straight at the camera with a clear view. Subject: kitten.
Said just before: (nothing)
The ad: Shakerz, sells Crunchy cat treats. It says: Every cat wants it. Possible last word: wants it.
Tone asked: funny.
This same ad already went out on other videos with these moves: gen-m11042017b1f (1), throw (1), camera (1), iris (1), thought (1). A brand wants each of its videos to feel different: prefer a move it has not had yet, as long as it truly fits this picture.

Pick one move (its id) and write the line(s) for it:
- wall: The frame falls back onto a white gallery wall and swings on its nail; the ad is the next picture along the wall. Line shape: Two beats. A teasing denial, then the admission. 4 to 8 words each. Example: This might not be an ad. / Oh wait. Actually, it is.
- camera: A camera viewfinder frames the shot, the shutter fires, and the camera roll's next photo is the ad. Line shape: A reaction to what is on screen, then an offer tied to the ad. Example: Oh, he's so cute. / Here's what you could give him.
- throw: A mouse grabs the frozen picture and throws it off screen; the next card slides in: the ad, with its product circled. Line shape: One unfinished sentence that the ad completes. Example: He's looking for...
- iris: A coloured iris closes on the subject's face while the line lands, shuts, and opens on [...]

input:
You are the last check before this bridge goes into a real video. It is a short motion-design transition: a video freezes, a line appears, and the picture is carried into an ad.
Watch it and list only real problems, with the second they happen:
- text cut off by the frame edge, overlapping other text, or hard to read on its background
- the cut-out subject broken: holes, a halo, missing limbs, a piece of background stuck to it
- blank, black or frozen frames where something should move; elements that jump instead of moving
- the ad not clearly visible, full screen, at the end
- a line that does not match what is on screen or what the ad sells
If nothing is wrong, ok is true, problems is empty and fix is "none". Do not invent problems to look useful.
The line: That sweet stare is not an ad. / Okay, it is. He wants crunchy treats.. The ad: Shakerz, Crunchy cat treats.
